root_cause: The focus trap incorrectly includes hidden focusable elements (e.g., the .retry button with display:none) in the list of focusable nodes, causing the tab focus to move beyond the modal's last visible control instead of wrapping to the first.
repair_strategy: Filter the focusable nodes returned by getFocusableNodes to exclude elements that are not rendered (offsetParent === null), ensuring only visible, focusable items are considered for wrapping behavior.
expected_accessibility_effect: Tabbing within the upload dialog will now cycle correctly among visible controls (#filename → #upload → #modal-close → #filename) and Shift+Tab will reverse, keeping focus inside the modal and preventing escape to page-level elements.
functional_risks: Elements that are intentionally zero‑size but still meant to be focusable could be inadvertently excluded (unlikely in this UI).
Custom visibility techniques that preserve offsetParent (e.g., off‑screen positioning) remain unaffected.
verification_requirements: After opening the modal, pressing Tab moves focus: #filename → #upload → #modal-close → then back to #filename.
Shift+Tab moves focus in the reverse order.
The hidden #retry button remains non‑focusable and does not affect the tab order.
Modal opening via mouse click continues to set initial focus to #filename.
Escape key still closes the modal and restores focus to the trigger button.
